**A Blues Scale (in the key of A)**  

| Scale Degree | Note | Interval from previous note |
|--------------|------|-----------------------------|
| 1 (root)     | A    | —                           |
| ♭3 (minor third) | C    | 3 semitones (m3)            |
| 4 (perfect fourth) | D    | 2 semitones (M2)            |
| ♭5 (diminished fifth / “blue” note) | Eb   | 1 semitone (m2)             |
| 5 (perfect fifth) | E    | 1 semitone (m2)             |
| ♭7 (minor seventh) | G    | 3 semitones (m3)            |
| 8 (octave)   | A    | 2 semitones (M2)            |

**Interval Pattern (in semitones):**  
`3 – 2 – 1 – 1 – 3 – 2`

So, in the key of A, the blues scale is:

```
A – C – D – Eb – E – G – A
```

This scale is built from the A minor pentatonic (A, C, D, E, G) with an added flat‑5 (Eb) that gives it its characteristic “bluesy” sound.
